Pendulum_lab experienced a real brief environmental perturbation (thermal, mechanical, or seismic) on Day 29 that affected only that instrument or location, while others were insulated or desensitized; the weak inter-instrument correlations reflect genuine spatial or instrumental heterogeneity in sensitivity to settlement-wide phenomena.

Pendulum_lab underwent a calibration drift or instrumental creep specific to that device starting on Day 29, independent of any external cause; each of the four instruments operates on its own isolated measurement scale, and weak inter-instrument agreement is baked into their design or mounting, not evidence of shared physics.

The 7-day periodicity detected in resonator instruments (resonator_lab r=0.354 at lag 14, resonator_obs r=0.358 at lag 13, both exceeding chance ±0.447) is real and reflects a genuine ~7-day environmental or settlement cycle (thermal, seismic, or activity-driven) to which resonators are selectively sensitive. Pendulums do not show this periodicity because they are more heavily damped or mechanically decoupled from the driving mechanism. The Day 29 pendulum_lab elevation is orthogonal to this resonator cycle and may reflect a local transient.

A time offset or phase lag between measurement streams masks a common signal; the Day 29 pendulum_lab elevation and the resonator 7-day periodicity are manifestations of the same underlying phenomenon, but viewed through different effective delays or sampling protocols, making them appear decorrelated.

Measurement protocol, operator technique, or site environmental differences (lab vs. observation location) introduce independent noise that dominates any true signal, and the Day 29 pendulum_lab elevation is a noise artifact or operator learning curve.

An unidentified systematic effect: weekly settlement activity or maintenance cycle, thermal conditioning, or unaccounted-for experimental or environmental scheduling that is coupled to the 7-day resonator periodicity and which also produced a transient on Day 29; requires access to settlement operational logs, maintenance schedules, thermal records, or operator shift rotation data to diagnose.
Residual: instrumental malfunction, electronic coupling between devices, or detector saturation producing organized but artifactual patterns.

Pendulum_lab experienced a real localized transient on Day 29 (thermal, vibrational, or seismic) to which it alone responded; inter-instrument decorrelation reflects genuine spatial/sensitivity heterogeneity, not measurement failure.

Pendulum_lab is undergoing an instrument-specific calibration drift or electrical offset that began on or around Day 29, independent of environment; each of the four instruments operates on its own measurement scale, and weak inter-instrument agreement is expected by design.

A genuine ~7-day environmental or settlement cycle (thermal, seismic, or activity-driven) drives the resonator instruments selectively; pendulums are too heavily damped or decoupled to show this periodicity, and the Day 29 pendulum_lab elevation is a distinct transient unrelated to the resonator cycle.

Measurement protocol, operator technique, or site environmental differences (lab vs. observation location) introduce large independent noise that dominates any true signal; the Day 29 pendulum_lab elevation is a noise artifact, operator shift, or site-specific disturbance unrelated to settlement physics.

A time offset or phase lag between measurement streams masks a common signal; the Day 29 pendulum_lab elevation and the resonator 7-day periodicity are manifestations of the same underlying phenomenon, but viewed through different effective delays or sampling protocols.

A settlement operational event (maintenance, thermal conditioning, power cycling, or recalibration protocol) occurred on or near Day 29 or follows a 7-day cycle; this event is coupled to both the Day 29 pendulum_lab elevation and the resonator 7-day periodicity.
Residual: an unconsidered mechanism (instrumental malfunction, electronic coupling between devices, detector saturation, or some other artifact).
Pendulum_lab and resonator_obs measure coupled responses to a genuine settlement-wide phenomenon with a consistent 3-day phase lag between readout chains
Electronic or calibration coupling between pendulum_lab and resonator_obs creates a spurious correlation; the r=0.949 is artifact, not signal

Pendulum_lab underwent a discrete calibration shift or instrumental drift starting around Day 29, visible as the 6-trial elevation; inter-instrument decorrelation is normal given independent measurement protocols, and the pendulum_lab ↔ resonator_obs correlation is coincidental or driven by a short-term anomaly in one or both instruments

A ~7-day environmental or operational cycle (thermal, seismic, or settlement activity-driven) preferentially drives the resonator instruments; pendulums are decoupled or too damped to resolve this periodicity, and the Day 29 pendulum_lab elevation is an unrelated local transient

Settlement operational or maintenance events on or near Day 29 and/or on a 7-day cycle drive both the pendulum_lab elevation and the resonator periodicity; external operational data (logs, maintenance schedules, thermal records) are needed to confirm or refute

Measurement protocol, operator technique, or environmental differences between lab and field observations introduce independent noise floors that suppress inter-instrument correlation; the pendulum_lab ↔ resonator_obs outlier is a statistical fluke or represents a narrow time window not generalizable to the full dataset
